name: Executive Order of November 21, 1892 adding land to the diminished Red Lake Reservation
nations: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It set apart as an addition to the diminished Red Lake reservation fractional section 33 of township 152 north, range 32 west, and fractional sections 4, 9, 16, 17, 19 and 20 and section 21 of township 151 north, range 32 west (Royce's schedule).
today: Royce lists this order as an addition to the Red Lake reservation, which had been diminished under the 1889 agreements (the Nelson Act cessions). No record was found that the added sections were later taken.

sources.title: Royce, Schedule of Indian Land Cessions, 1892 entries (cession 719)
sources.publisher: Bureau of American Ethnology, 18th Annual Report, part 2 (Royce, Indian Land Cessions, 1899), Internet Archive

sources.title: Legal Counsel's Certifications in Support of the Red Lake Nation's Application to Administer a Water Quality Standards Program (December 9, 2019)
sources.publisher: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians, filed with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency

openQuestions: Whether these added sections remain within the Red Lake reservation today was not checked against a current source.

The Indian Claims Commission's Red Lake dockets (for example Red Lake, Pembina and White Earth Bands v. United States) concern earlier cessions and the 1889 agreements; none opened addresses this addition.
2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Red Lake and Chippewa (Court of Claims index) and 'Red Lake 1892' (ICC); nothing on the 1892 addition.

nationVoice.nation: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nationVoice.summary: In its legal counsel's certifications to the EPA (December 9, 2019), the Band says it always held and never ceded the roughly 650,000-acre Diminished Reservation to which this order added land, that it refused allotment when negotiating the 1889 Agreement and resisted it for a decade until the federal government gave up, and that lands ceded in 1889 and 1902 were later partly restored by the 1945 Restoration Order.
